data.name: Hruditha
data.gender_notes: Hruditha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Hruditha is derived from the Sanskrit roots ‘hru’ meaning heart and ‘ditha’ meaning moving or causing to move. It signifies a woman who has the power to stir the heart and emotions of those around her. The name Hruditha carries the meaning “She who moves the heart” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi, Marathi. Parents who choose Hruditha usually hope their child will grow to embody she who moves the heart and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Hruditha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “She who moves the heart.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hruditha total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Hruditha is a unique and beautiful name that is rooted in Hindu culture. In Hindu mythology, the heart (hru) is considered the seat of emotions, love, and compassion. A woman named Hruditha embodies these qualities, stirring feelings of love, passion, and attachment in those around her. This name has a rich historical and cultural significance in India and is often used in Hindu literature and art to represent a noble and virtuous woman.
data.spiritual_significance: Hruditha's spiritual significance can be found in her ability to evoke emotions and stir the heart towards deeper connections with the divine. By moving the hearts of those around her, Hruditha reminds us of the power of love and compassion to transform and heal. In Hinduism, the heart is also seen as the center of consciousness and the source of inner wisdom and understanding. A woman named Hruditha may be seen as a spiritual guide or teacher, helping others to awaken their own inner wisdom and deepen their connection with the divine. Overall, Hruditha represents the transformative power of love, compassion, and the heart to connect us with the divine within ourselves and others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Hruditha, meaning 'he who dwells in the heart', symbolizes the divine presence within each individual. It emphasizes the importance of self-realization and self-love, as we are all embodiments of the divine.

historical_references.reference: Hruditha is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an epic Sanskrit poem originating in ancient India around 400 BCE. She is the wife of Bhima, one of the Pandava brothers.
In the Puranas, a genre of Indian texts, Hruditha is described as the mother of the great sage Vedavyas. The Puranas were composed between the 4th and 8th centuries CE.
